results.summary: This project implements a programmable clock generator that produces output frequencies from 100 Hz to 900 kHz based on a 50 MHz input clock. The output frequency is selected by a 4-bit radix input (1-9) and a 2-bit scale input that sets the base frequency range. The design uses a precomputed division factor and an 18-bit counter to generate a 50% duty-cycle square wave, with glitch-free updates occurring only at half-period boundaries. No external hardware is required, and the output is available on a single pin for observation with an oscilloscope or logic analyzer.

TinyCrypto-8 is an 8-bit pipelined ALU with hardware cryptography support, featuring a 12-bit instruction set that includes arithmetic, logic, shift, and LFSR-based crypto operations. Instructions are loaded serially through three input pins, and the 8-bit accumulator result is output on eight pins. The design is verified with a testbench that exercises ALU operations, flag updates, and crypto functions, and it requires no external hardware for basic operation. It is intended for educational or integration purposes, with optional microcontroller-based testing.

This design is an 8-channel programmable clock router that generates divided clock signals from a 50 MHz system clock. Each output channel can be independently configured via a 3-bit address, 4-bit division value, and a write strobe to select one of 16 counter bits as the clock source. The outputs are directly observable with a logic analyzer or oscilloscope, and no external hardware is required. The design is a straightforward utility for clock management in digital systems.

This project implements a ring oscillator physical unclonable function (RO-PUF) using 16 toggle flip-flops driven by an LFSR to create unique oscillators. Eight 12-bit counter pairs measure frequency variations over a 1000-cycle window, and a three-state FSM manages the measurement cycle, producing a single-bit response and a done flag. The design requires no external hardware and outputs debug information on six pins. It is notable for exploiting silicon manufacturing variation for hardware security primitives.

This project is a 4-channel PWM controller with SPI configuration, designed for half-bridge motor and LED driving. It includes configurable frequency, per-channel duty cycle and phase offset, dead-time insertion to prevent shoot-through, and fault protection that latches off outputs when the nFAULT input is asserted. The design requires an external SPI master and optionally a gate driver IC and power stage for motor control. It is notable for its comprehensive feature set and fault handling in a compact implementation.

This project implements a hardware triangle rasterizer that renders filled triangles to a 256x256 viewport on a 640x480 VGA display. It uses the edge-equation method with incremental evaluation to avoid per-pixel multiplications, and triangles are loaded serially via an 8-bit input with a valid strobe. The design requires a VGA PMOD and monitor, and an external microcontroller to send triangle data. It is notable for its efficient hardware rasterization suitable for embedded graphics.

QuadPulse is a 4-channel PWM generator ASIC for servo and DC motor control, providing jitter-free PWM signals with 8-bit duty cycle resolution. It supports four frequency modes (50 Hz to 20 kHz) and accepts runtime duty cycle updates via a 3-wire SPI interface. A hardware emergency stop pin instantly forces all outputs to zero. The design is intended for robotic systems and requires external servos, motors, or LEDs for testing, along with an SPI master.

This is an AC-coupled low noise amplifier designed to amplify EEG signals for brain-computer interface applications. It takes differential inputs (EEG_IN and EEG_REF) and produces an amplified output for low-frequency signals (1-100 Hz). The design is analog and requires external electrodes for actual EEG measurement, though testing can be done with a signal generator. The documentation is brief and lacks detailed specifications such as gain, noise figure, or power consumption.

This project implements a configurable analog clock generation unit with a voltage-controlled MUX selecting between 3, 5, and 7-stage ring oscillators on the Sky130 process. The selection is based on a DC voltage applied to an analog input, with eight 200mV thresholds across the 0-1.8V range. Additional test structures include frequency dividers, a capacitor-loaded oscillator, and a resistor-ladder voltage reference. Testing requires a lab DC power supply and oscilloscope, and the design is notable for its analog configurability and inclusion of characterization structures.

This design implements a 32-bit iterative multiply-accumulate (MAC) unit with a 7x8-bit multiplier, intended for tiny ML accelerators. A controller FSM manages partial sums and bias alignment across four training phases or one inference phase. The design is verified with cocotb tests comparing against a reference model, and it requires no external hardware beyond the Tiny Tapeout carrier. It is notable for its iterative architecture suitable for resource-constrained AI applications.
